title: dockato: water docked onto a DMSO of the box
purpose: `dockato` [@epsrmanual] builds larger molecules from `.ato` building blocks: copies of the first molecule of a docking file are bonded onto free sites of a docked file, removing one atom of each to form the new bond. Here a new ROT or DIH group has to be inserted among the 400 existing groups of a full box.
fortran: `dockato.f`: `dockato` (driver, parameters from command line or stdin), `rotatem`, `random_rotatem`, `search_unsaturated`, `find_valence`
system: The EPSR-test configuration `200DMSO400Water.ato`: 200 DMSO (atoms S, C, C, O, 6 H) and 400 water molecules (O1, H1, H1; SPC/E parameters [@berendsen1987]), 3200 atoms at 300 K in a cubic box of side 33.12 Å, a model of the DMSO-water mixtures of Soper and Luzar [@soperluzar1992]. Atom `atomd` of the new molecule is placed on `atomv`, the molecule is rotated so that its `atomdr` neighbour lies on the `atomvr` neighbour of `atomv` (equal bond lengths required), an optional second (dihedral) rotation about the new bond uses `atomdrr`/`atomvrr` (random angle in [dminrr, dmaxrr] from `ran1`, the Park-Miller generator with Bays-Durham shuffle [@parkmiller1988,@numrec1992], or a fixed dihedral that creates a DIH group when dminrr = dmaxrr), overlaps are tested with a distance factor, `atomd` and `atomvr` are removed and the new rotational group, bonds and atom types are updated. A water (O-H entries 1.10 Å) is bonded via its O1 to a methyl C of a DMSO in the box, replacing a methyl H.
inputs: `WaterOH110.ato` (as in ex83) and `200DMSO400Water.ato`. Run 1: site `C H H`, random 0-360°, factor 1.0 (`boxdmso`); run 2: overlaps allowed, fixed dihedral 90° referenced to S (`boxdmso2`); ndock = 1.
verification: Each run writes one new `.ato` file (coordinates, bonds, rotational groups, atom types and the random-number state), compared byte for byte with the stored Fortran output. Both outputs hold 3201 atoms and 401 rotational groups (400 methyl ROT groups of the box plus the new one); in `boxdmso2.ato` the first molecule has become an 11-atom DMSO-water unit with a DIH group.
